site.name: privacy-dashboard
site.summary: privacy-dashboard-clone Generic / abstract privacy management panel (not tied to any specific brand). Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Single-page panel: top account banner, section cards (activity data / personalized ads / location / search / devices), each card with a toggle + "Details" link + "Delete my X data" button; prominent danger zones for Download my data and Delete account; privacy-policy links in the footer | | `styles.css` | Cards, toggle switches, warning colors (yellow / red), confirmation modal styles | | `script.js` | Toggle coordination, delete second-confirmation modal, form mock submission, status indicators |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full privacy-dashboard system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The privacy dashboard offers a clean layout with responsive sidebar navigation and consistent toast notifications that provide immediate system feedback. However, several critical state synchronization bugs severely undermine user trust, notably privacy toggles that visually remain 'On' even when their status text changes to 'Off', and device cards that fail to update after a sign-out. Furthermore, z-index layering issues obscure confirmation modals behind side panels, hindering destructive actions. Note that testing covered 44% of interactive features, leaving specific retention limits and advanced ad personalization settings unverified.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the privacy-dashboard system, prioritizing data control toggles, deletion confirmation flows, and responsive layout.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will focus on the single-page dashboard application. It will systematically verify navigation elements, interact with activity filters and privacy checkup tools, toggle various data tracking settings to ensure state updates, and rigorously test the deletion and export modals.
assumptions: The site operates as a single-page application where sidebar links navigate to different sections or views within the same index.html page.
Data deletion and account actions trigger modal dialogs that require interaction.
Changes to toggles (e.g., turning off location history) will visually update status indicators on the page.
risk_hotspots: Data deletion confirmation modals (ensure they are accessible and can be canceled/confirmed).
Toggle switch states and their corresponding visual feedback.
Mobile layout usability, given the numerous small tap target warnings detected in the prescan.

phases.title: Navigation and Layout Verification
phases.objective: Ensure all primary navigation elements (sidebar and top nav) function correctly and layout is stable.
key_checks: Click sidebar links (Overview, Activity history, Data controls, etc.) and observe content updates or scroll behavior.
Check top navigation items (Privacy, Apps, Devices, Search, Account menu).
Verify visibility of the privacy score and summary cards.
exit_criteria: All main navigation areas have been clicked and their resulting state changes observed.

phases.title: Dashboard Widgets and Filters
phases.objective: Test the interactive widgets on the overview section.
key_checks: Interact with the 'Privacy checkup' section (e.g., click 'Start' or specific recommendations).
Test the 'Activity by category' time filters (30d, 90d, 1y buttons) to see if chart data changes.
Expand or interact with 'Recent activity' items.
exit_criteria: Time filters toggled and 'Privacy checkup' interactions completed.

phases.title: Data Control Toggles
phases.objective: Validate the functionality and UX of privacy toggles for different data categories.
key_checks: Locate sections for Search history, Browsing history, Location history, and Voice activity.
Toggle switches on and off for at least two categories.
Verify that turning a toggle off updates the UI (e.g., status text changes to 'Paused' or similar).
exit_criteria: At least two data control toggles have been successfully flipped and their state changes verified.

phases.title: Modals and Danger Zones
phases.objective: Thoroughly test destructive actions and data export flows to ensure safe user experience.
key_checks: Click 'Manage' or 'Delete' buttons on specific data history cards to trigger modals.
Interact with the 'Export data' and 'Delete account' buttons.
Attempt to close/cancel out of the triggered dialogs, then attempt a mock submission.
exit_criteria: All identified dialogs (up to 3) have been triggered, interacted with, and successfully dismissed.

phases.title: Mobile Usability Check
phases.objective: Re-evaluate critical interactions on a mobile viewport to check for tap target and layout issues.
key_checks: Verify how the sidebar navigation adapts (e.g., hamburger menu).
Open a deletion modal and ensure buttons are accessible and fit on screen.
Test toggle switches for tap target sizing.
exit_criteria: Navigation, one toggle, and one modal have been successfully operated in mobile view.

coverage_targets.pages: Fully explore index.html as a single-page app.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise navigation, time filters, state toggles, and all available modal dialogs.
coverage_targets.mobile: Focus on responsive navigation adaptation and modal usability.

notes: Since this is a demo environment, actual data won't be deleted, but UI mock submissions should be verified for appropriate success/error states.

findings.user_goal: Turn off tracking or data collection categories.
findings.problem: Privacy toggle switches visually fail to update to the 'Off' position when clicked, remaining blue and toggled right, even though the adjacent text and toast notifications indicate the setting is 'Off'.
findings.evidence: When clicking the 'Web & app activity' and 'Search history' privacy toggles, the status text updates to 'Off' and a toast appears, but the toggle component itself visually remains in the 'On' state.
findings.why_it_matters: Conflicting visual feedback on critical privacy controls severely erodes user trust. Users will be uncertain if tracking is actually disabled or if the system is broken.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the visual state of the toggle (CSS classes for background color and knob position) is strictly bound to the same underlying state variable that controls the text label and toast notification.

findings.user_goal: Confirm a destructive action like clearing search history or revoking app access.
findings.problem: Confirmation modals triggered from within side panels render beneath the side panel itself due to a z-index layering bug, obscuring the modal's text and action buttons.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Clear search' in the details panel, or 'Revoke access' in the mobile app details panel, successfully triggers a confirmation modal that is rendered behind the active slide-out panel.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot read the warnings or access the confirmation buttons, effectively trapping them or forcing them to blindly guess where to click to proceed or cancel.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the z-index of the modal wrapper and its backdrop to be higher than the slide-out details panels.
findings.source_hint: Modal overlay vs. side panel container

findings.user_goal: Secure an account by signing out of an unrecognized or old device.
findings.problem: After confirming a device sign-out, the device card does not update or disappear from the list, continuing to show 'Status: Trusted' and an active 'Sign out' button.
findings.evidence: Confirming a device sign-out displays a success toast ('Surface Laptop 6 signed out.'), but the corresponding device card does not update or disappear.
findings.why_it_matters: Security actions require unambiguous confirmation. When the UI fails to reflect the sign-out, users may panic, assuming the action failed and their account remains compromised.
findings.suggestion: Remove the device card from the DOM or update its status visually to 'Signed Out' with disabled action buttons immediately upon modal confirmation.

findings.user_goal: Revoke access for a connected application or sign out of a device.
findings.problem: There is a terminology mismatch between the buttons initiating an action ('Revoke', 'Sign out') and the primary confirmation button inside the resulting modal ('Delete').
findings.evidence: The confirmation modal for revoking app access and signing out a device uses the button label 'Delete' instead of matching the original action.
findings.why_it_matters: Users might hesitate or cancel the action out of fear that 'Delete' means permanently deleting their account or the app's internal data, rather than just severing the connection.
findings.suggestion: Match the modal's primary confirmation button text to the action being performed (e.g., 'Revoke Access' or 'Sign Out').
findings.source_hint: App revocation and Device sign-out modals

findings.problem: When the master 'Personalized ads' toggle is turned off, dependent settings like 'Interest profile' and 'Sensitive categories' remain fully visible and interactive.
findings.evidence: Turning off 'Personalized ads' updates the state, but dependent settings remain fully active and interactable (e.g., unchecking 'Alcohol' still shows a 'Setting turned off' toast).
findings.why_it_matters: This implies to users that their specific category preferences are still being used or tracked, confusing the mental model of how a global 'Off' switch functions.
findings.suggestion: Visually dim/disable child settings (or hide them entirely) when the parent master toggle is set to Off.

findings.user_goal: Close a data category details panel to return to the main dashboard.
findings.problem: The 'Close' button within the data category details side panel is completely non-functional.
findings.evidence: The 'Close' button (ux-40) in the data category details side panel is non-functional. Clicking it fails to dismiss the panel.
findings.why_it_matters: Users become trapped in the details view, obstructing their view of the dashboard and forcing them to reload the page or click outside elements if a backdrop dismiss isn't obvious.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the close button's click handler correctly fires the function that removes the side panel's visible CSS class.

findings.user_goal: Filter the activity history chart to view data over different timeframes.
findings.problem: Changing the time filter on the activity chart updates the button's visual active state and displays a confirmation toast, but the actual chart data remains completely static.
findings.evidence: Clicking the '90d' or '1y' time filter provides a toast notification ('Chart updated to 90d view.'), but the chart data itself (bars and numerical values) fails to update from the 30-day view.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the functional promise of the UI controls, making the chart useless for historical analysis and confusing users who rely on the data visualization.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the chart component re-renders with the appropriate dataset when a new time filter is selected.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the application or remove tags on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements fall below the recommended 44x44px minimum touch target size for mobile interfaces.
findings.evidence: The mobile hamburger menu button is 38x38px, side navigation links are 42px high, and interest remove ('x') buttons are 20x20px.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets increase the likelihood of accidental clicks or missed taps, causing friction for mobile users with varying manual dexterity.
findings.suggestion: Increase padding or set minimum height/width on mobile interactive elements to ensure they are at least 44x44px.
findings.source_hint: Mobile layout CSS, specifically buttons and navigation links
